articles.blurb: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users similar to offerings by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and others. The company is currently seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant that can write code, browse the web, control apps, and navigate devices on a user's behalf. Apple is working on agents that can plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs while coordinating specialized subagents along the way. The company's App Store has been dominated by AI agents, so it has introduced a new warning in the upcoming macOS 27.3 update that prompts users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.

articles.blurb: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029. Google's Project Suncatcher program is a long-term moonshot that aims to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into solar power. Its satellites each have the computing capacity of roughly the scale of a data center rack. The mission on New Glenn will deploy satellites into a Sun-synchronous orbit, where they will be able to receive nearly continuous solar energy.

articles.headline: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
articles.blurb: The BepiColombo mission is now preparing to swing into orbit around Mercury. The joint European-Japanese space mission aims to help scientists understand how Mercury formed so close to the Sun, why it has a magnetic field, and what makes up the frozen ice under the planet's permanently shadowed craters. The spacecraft will separate into two orbiters in early December. The orbiters will maneuver to different polar orbits around the planet, and science operations will begin in April next year.

articles.headline: PostgreSQL 19 Released!
articles.blurb: PostgreSQL 19 simplifies both administration and development for mission-critical workloads at scale. The release introduces the `REPACK (CONCURRENTLY)` command, which enables users to optimize tables for their current workload without disruption to ongoing operations. It also gives users better control over plan stability and query performance with the new pg_plan_advice extension. PostgreSQL 19 gives users new ways to manage their workloads without disruption and build applications that span multiple systems.

articles.headline: The most important number in AI
articles.blurb: The Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) is a measure of AI progress developed by Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization. It provides a single number that summarizes how well AI models do on benchmarks. It is designed to be continuously updatable, and researchers can use it to look at trends going back years and forecast things for future models. This post covers how the ECI is constructed, the challenges of benchmark selection, whether it makes sense to talk about 'model IQ', whether static benchmarks stay relevant as models get better, and much more.

Company sales start with only top executives and the board in the loop because leaks distract employees and weaken the seller's hand. Choosing an investment bank is a common leak point since banks that lose the pitch often talk. Many deals die early in the process, so keeping the circle tight avoids spooking customers unnecessarily. Bankers and lawyers also cost more than most founders expect.

articles.blurb: Requiring customers to enter a promo code can generate more sales than automatically applying the same discount. A study found that a 15% discount redeemed through a promo code converted at 1.45%, compared with 0.91% for an automatic discount. The small action makes customers feel like they earned the deal, increasing their sense of value and likelihood of redeeming it. The tactic works best for modest discounts of 10% to 15%, but the effort should remain minimal. Additional steps can create frustration and eliminate the benefit.

articles.headline: When influencers post sponsored content, your brand should...
articles.blurb: Your brand should actively support influencer content after it goes live rather than leaving all the engagement to creators. Have your social team comment on sponsored posts, reply to every comment, involve public-facing employees, share posts to Instagram Stories, and use reposts and tagged content to feature creator posts on your brand profile. For campaigns with multiple influencers, send creators links to each other's posts and encourage them to engage. Discuss these tactics with creators beforehand so everyone understands their role in promoting the partnership.

articles.headline: agentic-pmm Claude Skills (Website)
articles.blurb: Join the waitlist to get access to a free library of Claude skills for product marketers. The skills cover product positioning, GTM readiness, competitor tracking, and more. The library will become available to waitlist members on December 14.

articles.headline: Google Deep Review (Tool)
articles.blurb: Deep Review is an agentic AI system from Google Research that checks technical, scientific, and business documents for errors, inconsistencies, and weak claims. It supports PDFs and plain text. The tool provides two free document reviews per week.

articles.headline: Agentic Shopping - Maybe Nobody Wants This
articles.blurb: Agentic shopping faces consumer trust barriers as shoppers remain hesitant to let AI agents spend their money. While AI is used to research and compare products, retailers want to retain control of the actual purchase and customer relationship. Catalyst Brands is investing in loyalty programs to strengthen direct customer relationships across brands like JC Penney and Brooks Brothers.

articles.headline: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots
articles.blurb: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman oppose the idea of gradually handing control of society to AI as models become more powerful. Both believe humans must remain in charge but differ on how to prevent an accidental or intentional handover. Brockman stressed the growing need for better AI monitoring and security as models become harder to track through traditional chain-of-thought monitoring. Following a security breach, OpenAI redirected 25% of production engineers to security work.

articles.headline: PayPal Said Honey Followed Last-Click Attribution, Which Was the Whole Problem
articles.blurb: Last-click attribution can overstate the performance of advertising channels that capture sales rather than generate them. This is especially common in brand search, retargeting, coupon extensions, cart abandonment emails, and affiliate marketing. A 2015 eBay study found that turning off paid search ads had no significant impact on sales, even though attribution reports credited those ads with strong returns. Run incrementality tests to measure actual sales lift, exclude brand searches from automated campaigns, and revise affiliate terms to limit commissions for partners that only capture credit at checkout.

articles.blurb: An overview of product marketing and how PMMs drive research, positioning, GTM strategy, and enablement.

articles.blurb: More than half of Americans aged 16-69 play video games weekly and spend over 2B minutes a day gaming on TV.

articles.headline: TikTok Outpaces Instagram on Brand Engagement Despite Equal Reach
articles.blurb: TikTok turns the same reach into more engagement and faster follower growth, while Instagram Reels still lead every format on shares.

articles.headline: Kraken Parent Payward Acquires Tribe Capital to Enter Private Markets
articles.blurb: Payward, Kraken's parent, agreed to acquire Tribe Capital, a venture firm managing $2.7 billion chaired by Payward and Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi, with closing expected in Q1 2027 at an undisclosed price. The deal adds private-market investing to a vertical buildout that also includes the pending purchase of derivatives exchange Bitnomial, a $600 million acquisition of stablecoin payments firm Reap, and the buyout of Magic Labs' wallet business. Sethi's concurrent role as Tribe chair and Payward co-CEO positions the transaction as a formal consolidation of an already-integrated executive relationship rather than a standard external acquisition.

articles.headline: Ledger expands hardware hack investigation to Germany and UAE
articles.blurb: Ledger says new tampered devices in Berlin and Dubai are the same incident as the Southeast Asia campaign, with extra hardware that captures the recovery phrase during setup, and one case involves the newer Nano Gen5. It says there is no flaw in its chip or OS and no confirmed case from ledger.com. Two users claim a combined $604,000 in losses from a Dubai-authorized reseller, and Bitquery reports about $1.68M stolen from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, after earlier claims of $102M from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia. Ledger has not confirmed loss amounts and expects more devices to surface.

articles.headline: Lightspark Launches Agent Accounts for AI Agents
articles.blurb: Lightspark announced Agent Accounts, dedicated financial accounts that give AI agents the ability to hold balances and transact autonomously across multiple payment rails and currencies. The product targets developers building agents that need native payment capabilities, positioning Lightspark's Lightning-based infrastructure as the broadest multi-method solution for agent-to-agent and agent-to-human payments.

articles.headline: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement
articles.blurb: The Whale Orchestration Protocol runs on Ant's WhaleRTP platform and enables delivery-versus-payment between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds, developed under MAS's BLOOM initiative. Pilots with DBS and Franklin Templeton are complete. Separately, MAS issued S$100M of tokenized MAS Bills on November 6, Standard Chartered expanded tokenized deposits across Singapore and Hong Kong, and StraitsX, OCBC, and Standard Chartered finished an interoperability trial.

articles.headline: The Everything-App Race: Stickiness, Rev-Sharing, and Cross-Margin
articles.blurb: Robinhood, Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, Kraken, and Pump.fun are each expanding beyond their originating verticals, converging on a shared product surface spanning stocks, crypto spot, perps, prediction markets, and memecoins from divergent starting points across TradFi and crypto-native distribution. Three decisive factors: customer retention depth, rev-sharing structures that attract new users and retain whales, and cross-margin capability across the full product stack. No clear differentiation thesis has emerged.

articles.headline: Kalshi vs. Polymarket: Domain Experts Win
articles.blurb: Kalshi and Polymarket launched within months of each other, but Kalshi now posts roughly 4x the volume at 3x the valuation, with a $65B raise in talks versus Polymarket's unannounced $21B round. Kalshi's MIT math founders, with prior finance careers, sued the CFTC, won regulatory standing, then expanded into single-stock perps on 50+ companies, indices, and AI compute futures this year. Polymarket became a tab inside a memecoin application, sitting beside memecoins and perps, its standalone-exchange identity absorbed into a retail crypto product. Founder background drove the split: quant-finance founders built toward prediction markets as a regulated asset class, while operator-type founders built toward distribution as the product.

articles.headline: Why Bitcoin needs capital markets and how Stacks is building them
articles.blurb: Bitcoin lacks yield, credit, and trading markets, and holders shouldn't have to hand over BTC to earn. Stacks' Bitcoin staking is live, with bonds targeting 3% annual yield paid in BTC from miners' Proof of Transfer commitments. The first two bonds drew 735 BTC, with Bullish staking in Bond 3 and Anchorage offering custody. In 2027, Stacks plans an open auction through PoX-6 and borrowing stablecoins against staked BTC. STX is required at 5% of the BTC value, and SIP-034 raised block capacity up to 30x, with a 100x goal.

articles.headline: Morpho and Aave are in a full BD war
articles.blurb: Onchain lending now depends on distribution, partnerships, and integrations through neobanks, wallets, and exchanges, not just a good app. Morpho is plugging into apps people already use: Coinbase Borrow in New York, OKX Wallet on X Layer, earn products at Ledger, Bitso, Pulsar, Abra, and Deel, Robinhood Stock Tokens as collateral, and new APIs. Aave is pursuing infrastructure partners and new collateral through V4: Circle Mint, Privy, and Base for fintechs, Ethena Pay's Earn+, cirBTC, PAXGy, mWIN, and Coinbase tokenized stocks, plus the Avon acquisition for fixed-rate lending. V3 Core going blue-chip only pushes new assets to V4. The real race is owning tokenized non-crypto assets through early issuer partnerships, and most onchain lending will likely run on one of the two.

articles.blurb: Microsoft and Intel have announced an expansion of their collaboration under a long-term agreement to advance Azure cloud and AI infrastructure. Microsoft will become the first company to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its first-party silicon and secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids server CPUs. The partnership also covers system-level optimizations using CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist Technology, and Intel Trust Domain Extensions for confidential computing.

articles.headline: Legacy software may be holding back enterprise AI
articles.blurb: Google Cloud's Jeanette Manfra argues that maintenance burdens and vendor lock-in are limiting organizations' AI ambitions. She cites Google-commissioned research in which 78% of surveyed technology leaders said maintaining legacy systems diverts resources from AI, and advocates greater vendor choice and stronger security requirements in procurement.

articles.headline: IT leaders are deciding which decisions machines can make on their own
articles.blurb: IT leaders and chief information officers are navigating the challenges of deploying autonomous IT and generative AI tools in high-security environments. While rules-based automation and large language models help synthesize large volumes of data and accelerate cybersecurity defenses, agencies face significant hurdles regarding data readiness, over-trust in AI results, and classifying sensitive information. Organizations are addressing these challenges by establishing localized large language models, data governance structures, and strict human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

articles.headline: Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior
articles.blurb: Microsoft has introduced agent controls, a managed Azure service designed to help enterprises centrally define, manage, and evaluate policies governing AI agent behavior. Built on the open-source Agent Control Specification and Agent Hooks, the service brings runtime governance to heterogeneous AI agent fleets without requiring organizations to build custom policy infrastructure. It evaluates agent actions and content using content safety classifiers, LLM judges, and deterministic Rego rules.

articles.headline: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux
articles.blurb: Google's AI and Infrastructure team built Sashiko, an open-source, agentic code review system powered by Gemini designed to help maintainers review Linux kernel patches. The system separates bug finding from verification using parallel specialist sessions and per-bug deep checks. Data from seven months of production use on kernel mailing lists show that Sashiko completes about 1,200 reviews daily and correlates with a 35 percent drop in 60-day follow-up fixes for merged commits.

Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

articles.headline: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?

But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.headline: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California.
